My first AllTrails hike was fortunately on a beautiful sunny holiday Monday.  The trail was busy but not crowded.  When I arrived at the Glen Rouge Campground parking lot by the trailhead, it was full.  But drivers were lined up and patiently waiting, so as cars exited the lot, one by one each waiting car was able to park.  

Trail signage could be a bit confusing.  The Mast Trail on AllTrails is a loop, whereas the "official" Parks Canada Mast Trail is linear (see at https://www.pc.gc.ca/en/pn-np/on/rouge/activ/randonnee-hiking/mats-mast).  So the signage on site does not quite match with the trail defined in All Trails.  Also, a Parks Canada ranger I met on the trail explained that they have recently had lands of Park transferred to them from the Zoo, the City of Toronto, and the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA).  So trail signage is a mix of all these different organizations.  But with the app on my phone it was easy to stay on the AllTrails version of the trail.  

The trail had some inclines and multiple treefalls.  It was fine for hiking, but I believe not suitable for strollers, and would be challenge for mountain bikes. There are lots of side trails that make it extra interesting.

The Parks Canada ranger explained that a big new Visitor Centre is planned for the Zoo Road access point, to be ready around 2025.  And that signage and trail improvements are planned to build a linked network of trails from Stouffville in the north, all the way down to Rouge Beach on Lake Ontario.

So my husband and I have never been here before and we got totally lost. Luckily we had the AllTrails app to guide us back. Unfortunately the map wasn’t updated and there were some parts that were eroded due to the river and new paths were created. You can see on my recording info the detours that we took! Would definitely do this trial again but we will keep a closer eye on our map. The trial where we where was very very steep at some parts and not safe for children. Now and then you’ll see other hikers so you know you’re still on the right trail as there are off shoots here and there. Using this app certainly helped me navigate through the trail. Make sure to be hydrated. I saw a deer grazing through towards the ravine for a drink of water; it was lovely to see.
This was a great trail! It’s very covered also a lot of bugs but still worth it! There are a lot of side trails that you can take to make this more of a moderate hike.

With the lobe from 0.5 km to 2.2 km or so (going clockwise) - following the elevation guide, closed for environmental reasons, this is a much shorter hike. Orange snow fence / signage at both ends of the closed section. The far end of the closed section comes out at the crossroads where the two loops meet and you have the choice of the West ridgeline hike or the East descent further into the valley which was quite muddy and had flooded recently as there were a few ice flows .more than 100m from Little Rouge Cr. The old Caper Valley Ski Hill that goes NE to SW at the 3km mark is a serious hill, as per the elevation guide. 
Only recommendation is that you park at the Twyn Rivers lot. The lot at Kingston Rd was all but full. You can access the top end of this trall by heading West from the Twyn Rivers lot and cross the bridge on Twyn Rivers and then about 300m back East in to meet this trail.

A great hike that I’m looking forward to doing in the summer months. As there is no winter maintenance for Rouge Park, there was a LOT of dog droppings and it was extremely slippery – particularly when you get to the uphill areas. The downfall per each season, however, is the lack of signage throughout (from beginning to end). At one point, there is a fork in the road (three different trails) and you’re not quite sure which one to go down. In the summer, this wouldn’t be a major issue, but in the winter it may have been risky. My friend slipped 3 times, but I found it fairly intermediate in the winter. Definitely do it in the summer if you’re new to hiking!!
Nice forested walk with litigation side trails to explore.

The route shown on the map actually includes the Riverside Trail (which has not been maintained) but continues to be very popular with trail runners.  The Mast Trail Loop being bounded between the Little Rouge Creek & Rouge River enjoys ridges that overlooks these waterways.  As a result numerous secondary trails exist that create challenging hill climbs from the low lying areas to the tops of he ridges.  The former Caper Valley Ski hill is just one of them. These primary and secondary trails if linked correctly create a challenging 10 km loop with six aggressive hill climbs.
A nice foested trail that makes you feel like you are in a remote area and not the city. Some parts of the route are closed so route adjustments may be necessary.

Some obstacles and in forest on the hill you can run around off-trail and run on branch and tree.  Still very muddy and wet on the ground with some fallen trees, but that's what's trail running for.  Definitely come back to explore and run again.

This trail blows all other Toronto trails I've walked out of the water. This is a real forest. Real animals (other than squirrels) live here (including lots of birds). Although you never get away from the hum of the highway, I can see why they almost turned this area is being turned into a national urban park.

The trail gets a fair bit of use. A downside in a more nature setting but perhaps gives you a bit of comfort in an urban park. 

One negative: the trail needs signage and maps!

Great forest trail close to Toronto with a surprising amount of wildlife.  The forest seemed open and inviting.  The sound of the highway nearby was the only thing to remind you you were in the city.  We stayed close to the ridge line which gave interesting views through the forest into the valley.  The trail had a number of branches and side trails to wander down.
Great trail for running. Good straight aways, challenging hill climb and a good length for a short high intensity run.

Nice, well groomed trails which were easy to navigate. There are various small side trails to explore, which all connect back to the main trail and were easy to figure out. I was here at 7a.m. and there were already numerous people on the trail (dog walkers, runners etc.), by the time I finished there were lots of people and dogs on the trail. There are a few river access points which was nice and dogs can get into the river and cool down, but be careful as there are fast currents throughout the river in some parts.

Note: parts of the trail are hilly and there are some significant inclines to navigate through the northern loop of the trail. Would recommend but suggest coming early morning to beat some of the 'trail traffic'!

Great workout - very hilly.  Not a very exciting trail as far as scenery goes, very average forest and occasional glimpses of the Rouge, it was super hot so there wasn't even many birds around.  Free parking.

Amazing trail! I go with family. So far we've tried two of the trails. The first one was difficult with lots of incline. I loved it but can't say my sister did lol.
